body.statement: Can the handle \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{fin}}\) establish, uniformly over \(\mathfrak M\), exact ties, arbitrary balanced deterministic baseline lattices, local action displacements of order \(m^{-1/2}\), and unequal inclusion probabilities, that the finite Horvitz--Thompson action regret on \(T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}\) differs from the continuous-coarea Gaussian boundary quadratic form of \(G_{\infty}\) by \(o(m^{-1})\) in probability over the split, and that the contrast between \(T_n^{\mathrm{full}}\) and \(T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}\) has no additional lattice or inclusion correction at order \(m/n^2+1/(nm)\)?
body.justification: This is the proof boundary on which the advertised second-order constant is valid or must acquire a finite-randomization correction.
body.gap: Li and Ding provide a first-order random-partition central limit theorem, and Wang and Li provide quantitative Gaussian control for best-choice rerandomization; neither controls score-weighted moving-boundary moments at this scale.
body.consumer: A positive answer validates smooth pilot rules on integer-valued manufacturing baselines; a negative answer identifies the correction planners must include.
